place_fields.summary: Bhujanga Park in Ajjarakadu, Udupi is a public green space with walking lanes and seating; reporting also identifies a historic radio tower in the park and describes it as a recreational space used by local residents.
place_fields.best_time: Evening is a practical time to visit; the park's restored radio tower was reported as operating from 5:30pm to 8:00pm.

planning_attributes.description: A public park in Ajjarakadu, Udupi with walking areas, seating and a restored historic radio tower.
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: The park contains a radio tower built in 1938; it was restored and returned to service in 2020. Reporting also notes a Gandhi memorial in the park.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: The park is in Ajjarakadu, Udupi; published local directions describe reaching Ajjarakadu from the Taluk Office stop and continuing on foot or by auto-rickshaw.

place_fields.summary: Kidiyoor Dakke is a tourist attraction in Udupi, Karnataka. Published listings place it at 8PJ7+VVM, Udupi 576103 and describe it as a quiet, scenic place; a local tourism page describes it as a calm riverside spot associated with the Swarna River.
place_fields.best_time: Evening is a reasonable time for a short scenic stop based on descriptions emphasizing a calm atmosphere; no authoritative visiting-hour restriction was found.

planning_attributes.description: A small scenic tourist attraction in the Udupi area associated with a riverside setting.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: Published listings give the location as 8PJ7+VVM, Udupi, Karnataka 576103.
planning_attributes.notes: Available web sources are mainly local/place-listing sources; detailed official site information was not located.

place_fields.summary: The Group of Monuments at Hampi is the surviving monumental landscape of the Vijayanagara capital in Karnataka. UNESCO describes more than 1,600 surviving remains including temples, royal and sacred complexes, fortifications, water structures and other archaeological features across the property.
place_fields.best_time: A cooler part of the day is preferable for walking the extensive open archaeological landscape; no single official best visiting time was identified in the cited sources.

planning_attributes.description: A large UNESCO World Heritage cultural property comprising extensive Vijayanagara-era archaeological remains, including temples, royal complexes, fortifications and water structures.
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: Hampi was the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire from the 14th to 16th centuries and was heavily destroyed after the Battle of Talikota in 1565. UNESCO inscribed the property as a World Heritage Site in 1986.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: The property is in Hampi, Karnataka; the cited UNESCO and Government of India sources identify the site and its regional location but do not provide a single visitor route in the supplied evidence.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: The UNESCO management assessment notes pressures from development, encroachment and visitor-related infrastructure, so visitors should follow site-management rules and protect the archaeological remains.
planning_attributes.notes: The supplied coordinates are preserved exactly from request metadata; they differ slightly from the broader coordinates published by UNESCO for the property.
